subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the person who appears as the male performer at center stage (originally an older Chinese man in a dark blue Mao suit and matching cap) in the original footage, now replaced by the person in <Picture 2>: a Black man with the exact face of the reference portrait, wearing a yellow Lakers #24 basketball jersey with purple arm sleeves, matching yellow-purple shorts, white socks and white-purple sneakers. The facial identity, hair and costume of <Subject 1> come only from <Picture 2> and stay consistent from the first frame to the last.
<Picture 1> is the replaced keyframe of this segment: it locks the composition, the scene, the lighting, the starting pose of every person and the appearance of all non-target people; the generated video starts exactly from this frame.
<Video 1> is the source segment of the original footage and serves as the motion reference. Only the actions, poses, gestures, camera framing, expressions and second-by-second timing are taken from it; the original performer's identity, face, hair and costume are NOT carried over, and no on-screen text, no subtitles, no captions, no logos, no watermarks and no TV-station bugs anywhere in the frame — any text, subtitle or logo visible in the source footage must NOT appear in the generated video. Its synchronized audio track is reused as <Audio 1>.
<Audio 1> is the synchronized audio track of <Video 1>, reused 1:1 as the complete final audio track of the target video.

summary:
[reference generation + audio reuse] The target video reproduces the source segment <Video 1> with <Subject 1> replacing the corresponding original performer(s): the target person's actions, poses, gestures, body orientation, weight shifts and timing follow <Video 1> second by second and are NOT changed, re-choreographed, sped up or slowed down; the scene, composition, lighting and all other people are preserved exactly; no on-screen text, no subtitles, no captions, no logos, no watermarks and no TV-station bugs anywhere in the frame — any text, subtitle or logo visible in the source footage must NOT appear in the generated video. <Audio 1> is reused in full as the final audio track.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the facial identity, hair and costume from <Picture 2> are retained unchanged from first frame to last.
<Picture 1> (segment keyframe): attribute_transfer - the composition, scene, lighting and the non-target people are carried over unchanged; only the target person's identity comes from the reference portrait(s).
<Video 1> (motion and timing): attribute_transfer - the actions, poses, gestures, weight shifts, expressions and timing are transferred exactly, while the original performer's identity and any on-screen text, subtitles or logos are NOT carried over.
<Audio 1>: fully_copy - <Audio 1> is reused 1:1 as the target video's complete final audio track.

detailed_description:
The target video is a realistic continuous shot with no cuts, matching the source segment's framing and camera work. <Audio 1> plays from the very first frame at an unchanged tempo. The video starts exactly from the keyframe image <Picture 1>.
[Shot 1] Three performers dance in sync on stage. <Subject 1> is at center, flanked by two male backup dancers in black uniforms (the left one wears a peaked cap and sunglasses, the right one is bald with sunglasses). They perform energetic synchronized choreography: knee bends, side steps, arm swings and rhythmic bouncing, all landing on the beat of the music.
the target person's actions, poses, gestures, body orientation, weight shifts and timing follow <Video 1> second by second and are NOT changed, re-choreographed, sped up or slowed down. every other person in the scene keeps their original face, hair, costume and movement exactly as in the source footage and the keyframe image, completely unchanged; no new person is added and no background person is removed or altered. no on-screen text, no subtitles, no captions, no logos, no watermarks and no TV-station bugs anywhere in the frame — any text, subtitle or logo visible in the source footage must NOT appear in the generated video. Neither the target person's face, hair or costume, nor the scene and lighting, changes from the first frame to the last.

overall_soundscape:
The ambience and any dialogue copied from <Audio 1> run through the whole video unchanged; nothing is added, removed or re-timed.

non_diegetic_music:
<Audio 1> is directly reused as the complete audio track of the target video, with nothing added, removed, re-timed or replaced.
